mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an easing monetary policy that reduces the risk-free rate, lowering the discount rate for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances (UNRATE > 4.5% for 2 consecutive months), or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline in the prior month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline in the prior month, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising), the Federal Reserve's policy rate hikes compress equity valuations by increasing discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising, or the Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past 3 months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate output and profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines by at least 0.5% over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% year-over-year signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%), or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market contraction, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decline and UNRATE decline in the prior month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS and UNRATE both decline in the prior month, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply chain disruption regime (INDPRO < 95 and declining), manufacturing bottlenecks reduce corporate output and increase costs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 95 and declining, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.
